reason: E2 shows that Ti addition to a CoNiFe alloy leads to coherent (CoNi)3Ti precipitates after annealing and full heat treatment, with a 357% hardness increase, supporting the precipitation strengthening premise. However, the cited evidence involves a CoNiFe-based system, not a Ti-Ni-primary alloy, and does not address elevated-temperature mechanical properties or the specific Ni3Ti phase claimed. E1 and E3 provide no direct support for the key premises.
premises: Ti addition to CoNiFe alloys enables precipitation of coherent (CoNi)3Ti phase upon aging
Precipitation of (CoNi)3Ti provides significant strengthening (large hardness increase)
Aging after solution treatment can produce coherent precipitates in Ti-containing high-entropy alloys
Nanoscale coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding, enhancing high-temperature strength
